topStory.headline: UMass Dartmouth Student Comic Sparks Boston-Area 'A.I. Slop' Backlash
topStory.summary:
Caitlyn Harrington, a University of Massachusetts Dartmouth student, created a viral comic criticizing her campus's A.I.-generated social media posts, according to the Boston Globe. The critique of artificial images promoting campus events like a "Pizza and Painting Night" has sparked a broader movement against what critics call "A.I. slop" across the Boston area.

The backlash extends beyond higher education to police departments, political campaigns, and local businesses, all facing public criticism for using obviously artificial imagery in official communications. When UMass Dartmouth used A.I.-generated art for campus events or when local police departments shared A.I. videos, these institutions triggered reactions from communities that perceived the content as inauthentic.

A 250,000-member Facebook group has formed dedicated to identifying A.I.-generated content. The movement highlights generational differences in A.I. literacy, with younger audiences recognizing common indicators of artificial content including unnatural smoothness, text errors, and impossible architectural features. The emergence of organized opposition suggests a cultural shift toward demanding transparency about artificial content in public communications.

stories.headline: Dartmouth Celebrates 70th Anniversary of A.I.'s Founding
stories.summary: Dartmouth hosted events on February 26-27 marking 70 years since the 1956 Summer Research Project that coined "artificial intelligence," according to Dartmouth News. The McGuire Family Prize was awarded to Hany Farid, a digital forensics expert who pioneered techniques for detecting manipulated images and deepfakes.

stories.headline: Pace University Hosts Enterprise A.I. Conference
stories.summary: Morgan Stanley's A.I. executive headlined Pace University's Spring Actionable AI Conference, according to Pace University. Executives from Google, Zoom, and Heineken discussed overcoming integration challenges and managing A.I. risks in enterprise settings. The event focused on practical A.I. implementation across industries.

stories.headline: Reuters Institute Examines A.I. Impact on Newsroom Fact-Checking
stories.summary: An Oxford conference explored how A.I. is reshaping journalism, from investigative reporting tools to fact-checking automation, according to the Reuters Institute. Speakers noted A.I.-generated misinformation now comprises 16% of fact-checked claims in Brazil, up from 7% the previous year.

stories.headline: UK Study Identifies 'Shadow A.I. University' Among Students
stories.summary: Queen Mary University research identifies informal student networks sharing A.I. tools and prompts outside institutional oversight, according to Wonkhe. The study warns this creates a two-tier learning experience based on digital access and A.I. literacy levels.

stories.headline: New Zealand Student Publication Releases Transparent A.I. Policy
stories.summary: Te Waha Nui announced clear guidelines for A.I. use in student journalism, permitting transcription and translation assistance while prohibiting A.I.-generated content, according to Te Waha Nui. The policy emphasizes human oversight and transparency in all A.I. applications.

stories.headline: Bucks County School Districts Implement Varied A.I. Approaches
stories.summary: Bucks County, Pennsylvania school districts are implementing different strategies for A.I., from think tanks to pilot programs, according to Technical.ly. Central Bucks launched a Microsoft Copilot pilot with data protection measures, while other districts focus on teacher training and ethical guidelines.
